set_title: Named triads I: Charcot triad, Reynolds pentad, Virchow triad, Whipple triad and Cushing triad
stem: A 36-year-old woman has episodes of sweating and confusion before breakfast. During one, her glucose is 38 mg/dL, and the symptoms resolve after IV dextrose. Insulin and C-peptide levels are elevated.
oneliner: 36F, fasting sweating and confusion + glucose 38, relieved by dextrose → ?

whyNot.A: Charcot triad is fever, jaundice and RUQ pain; hers are **fasting sweating and confusion**
whyNot.B: Virchow triad lists thrombosis risks; hers is **glucose 38 relieved by dextrose**
whyNot.C: Cushing triad is hypertension, bradycardia, irregular breathing; she has **glucose 38**
whyNot.E: Reynolds pentad is cholangitis with shock and confusion; she has **glucose 38**

why: Low glucose, hypoglycemic symptoms and relief with **dextrose** are Whipple triad, confirming true hypoglycemia. High insulin and C-peptide suggest an insulinoma.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Low glucose, symptoms, relief with glucose

idea.rule: Low glucose, symptoms, relief with glucose = true hypoglycemia.

set_title: Muscle and calcium signs: Chvostek sign, Trousseau sign of hypocalcemia, Gowers sign, Grip myotonia and Post-exercise facilitation
stem: A 46-year-old woman has numbness around her mouth and hand cramps 2 days after total thyroidectomy. When the examiner taps over the cheek just in front of her ear, the corner of her mouth twitches. Calcium is 6.8 mg/dL with albumin 4.0 g/dL.
oneliner: 46F, post-thyroidectomy perioral numbness + cheek tap twitches the mouth, Ca 6.8 → ?

whyNot.A: Trousseau needs cuff-induced carpal spasm; hers is a **tap in front of the ear**
whyNot.B: Gowers is climbing the legs to stand; hers is **a facial twitch on tapping**
whyNot.D: Grip myotonia is slow handshake release; hers is **a facial twitch on tapping**
whyNot.E: Facilitation is strength improving with effort; hers is **a twitch on tapping the cheek**

why: Tapping the facial nerve in front of the ear twitches the facial muscles. Low calcium raises neuromuscular excitability, here **after thyroidectomy** with parathyroid injury.

idea.rule: Facial twitch on tapping ahead of the ear = Chvostek, hypocalcemia.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Tapping facial nerve twitches the face
BP cuff inflation causes carpal spasm
Climbs hands up legs to stand
Strength and reflexes improve with effort

set_title: Muscle and calcium signs: Chvostek sign, Trousseau sign of hypocalcemia, Gowers sign, Grip myotonia and Post-exercise facilitation
stem: A 55-year-old man has tingling around his mouth 1 day after parathyroidectomy for an adenoma. A blood pressure cuff inflated above systolic pressure for 3 minutes makes his hand flex at the wrist with fingers pulled together (Trousseau sign). ECG shows a prolonged QT interval.
oneliner: 55M, day 1 after parathyroidectomy + cuff-induced carpal spasm, long QT → ?
ask: Which electrolyte abnormality best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Excess magnesium causes weakness and lost reflexes; he has **tingling and carpal spasm**
whyNot.B: Hyperkalemia causes weakness and peaked T waves; his ECG shows **a prolonged QT interval**
whyNot.C: Hyponatremia causes confusion and seizures; his findings follow **parathyroidectomy** with carpal spasm
whyNot.D: Hypokalemia causes weakness and U waves; his surgery and **QT prolongation** point to calcium

why: Ischemia from the cuff unmasks the raised nerve excitability of low calcium. Hungry bone syndrome after **parathyroidectomy** is a classic setting.

idea.rule: Cuff-induced carpal spasm = Trousseau = hypocalcemia, with long QT.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Tapping facial nerve twitches the face
BP cuff inflation causes carpal spasm
Climbs hands up legs to stand
Strength and reflexes improve with effort

set_title: Face and atopy signs: Dennie-Morgan lines, Allergic shiners, Transverse nasal crease, Hutchinson sign and Hertoghe sign
stem: A 47-year-old woman has had 6 months of weight gain, constipation, cold intolerance and dry skin. The outer third of both eyebrows is missing (Hertoghe sign). Her pulse is 54/min, and her ankle reflexes relax slowly.
oneliner: 47F, weight gain + constipation + missing outer eyebrows → hormone?
ask: Deficiency of which hormone best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: Cortisol deficiency causes hypotension and hyperpigmentation; she has **bradycardia and slow reflex relaxation**
whyNot.B: Low parathyroid hormone gives tetany; she has **cold intolerance and weight gain**
whyNot.C: ADH deficiency causes polyuria and thirst; she has **constipation and bradycardia**
whyNot.D: Aldosterone deficiency gives hyperkalemia and hypotension; she has **bradycardia and weight gain**

why: Loss of the lateral third of the eyebrows is Hertoghe sign, seen in hypothyroidism. **Weight gain, constipation, bradycardia and slow reflex relaxation** show thyroid hormone deficiency.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Vesicles on the tip of the nose
Zoster of V1 with eye risk
Loss of outer third of eyebrows

idea.rule: Lateral eyebrow loss + weight gain + cold intolerance = Hertoghe = hypothyroidism.
also: TSH is high in primary hypothyroidism
Hashimoto thyroiditis is the common cause

set_title: Fundus signs: Cherry-red spot, Hollenhorst plaque, Cotton-wool spots, AV nicking and Blood and thunder fundus
stem: A 54-year-old man with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes has fluffy white retinal patches with feathery borders on funduscopy. His vision is unaffected.
oneliner: 54M, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes + fluffy white retinal patches → ?

options.B: New vessels growing from the disc
options.E: Blot hemorrhages in the inner retina

whyNot.A: Lipid deposits are hard exudates with **sharp yellow borders**, not fluffy white patches
whyNot.B: New vessels look like fine red networks; his lesions are **fluffy white patches**
whyNot.D: Drusen are yellow deposits in macular degeneration; his patches are **fluffy and white**
whyNot.E: Blot hemorrhages are red; his lesions are **white with feathery borders**

why: Fluffy white patches are cotton-wool spots: microinfarcts of the retinal nerve fiber layer with axoplasmic buildup, seen in diabetes, hypertension and HIV.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Bright yellow plaque in retinal artery
Widespread hemorrhages, swollen veins, disc edema

idea.rule: Fluffy white retinal patches = nerve fiber layer infarcts.

set_title: Thyroid signs: Lid lag, Pretibial myxedema, Woltman sign, Pemberton sign and Thyroid bruit
stem: A 31-year-old woman with 8 kg weight loss, tremor and heat intolerance is asked to follow the examiner's finger slowly downward. Her upper eyelids trail behind the eyeballs, exposing white sclera above the iris.
oneliner: 31F, weight loss, tremor, heat intolerance + upper lid trails eye on downgaze → ?

whyNot.A: Pretibial myxedema is a shin plaque; her finding is at the **upper eyelids**
whyNot.B: Woltman is slow ankle reflex relaxation; hers is **eyelid movement on downgaze**
whyNot.C: Pemberton needs arm raising with facial flushing; she **follows a finger downward**
whyNot.E: A bruit is heard over the gland; hers is **eyelid lag on downgaze**

why: Upper lids that trail the globe on downgaze are lid lag, from sympathetic overdrive of Muller muscle in hyperthyroidism.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Upper lid lags as eye looks down
Arms raised cause facial flushing, distress
Bruit heard over diffusely enlarged thyroid

idea.rule: Upper lid trails the eye on downgaze = lid lag; thyroid hormone excess.

set_title: Thyroid signs: Lid lag, Pretibial myxedema, Woltman sign, Pemberton sign and Thyroid bruit
stem: A 48-year-old woman has fatigue, constipation, cold intolerance and a hoarse voice. When the examiner taps her Achilles tendon, the foot plantarflexes briskly but returns to neutral very slowly.
oneliner: 48F, fatigue, cold intolerance, hoarse voice + slow ankle reflex relaxation → ?

whyNot.A: Lid lag is eyelid delay; hers is **slow reflex return at the ankle**
whyNot.B: Pretibial myxedema is a skin plaque; hers is a **slow reflex relaxation**
whyNot.D: Pemberton needs raised arms and flushing; hers is an **Achilles tap**
whyNot.E: A bruit is heard over the gland; hers is a **slow-relaxing reflex**

why: Slow relaxation of the ankle reflex is the Woltman sign of hypothyroidism. Slower muscle calcium reuptake prolongs the relaxation phase.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Upper lid lags as eye looks down
Arms raised cause facial flushing, distress
Bruit heard over diffusely enlarged thyroid

idea.rule: Delayed relaxation of the ankle reflex = Woltman; hypothyroidism.
also: Contraction speed is normal; relaxation is slow

set_title: Thyroid signs: Lid lag, Pretibial myxedema, Woltman sign, Pemberton sign and Thyroid bruit
stem: A 38-year-old woman with exophthalmos and heat intolerance has waxy, orange-peel plaques over both shins.
oneliner: 38F, exophthalmos, heat intolerance + waxy orange-peel shin plaques → ?

options.C: Immune complex deposition in dermal vessels

whyNot.B: Venous stasis causes brown pigmentation; she has **exophthalmos and heat intolerance**
whyNot.C: Immune complexes cause palpable purpura, not **waxy shin plaques with exophthalmos**
whyNot.D: Generalized myxedema is hypothyroid; she is **hyperthyroid with exophthalmos**
whyNot.E: Histamine release gives urticaria; her lesions are **fixed waxy plaques**

why: Graves antibodies also activate TSH receptors on dermal fibroblasts, which deposit glycosaminoglycans and give waxy shin plaques alongside exophthalmos.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Upper lid lags as eye looks down
Arms raised cause facial flushing, distress
Bruit heard over diffusely enlarged thyroid

idea.rule: Waxy shin plaques in Graves = TSH-receptor antibodies on fibroblasts.

set_title: Thyroid signs: Lid lag, Pretibial myxedema, Woltman sign, Pemberton sign and Thyroid bruit
stem: A 60-year-old woman has a long-standing painless neck swelling that moves with swallowing; its lower edge cannot be felt above the clavicles. When she raises both arms above her head, within a minute her face flushes, her neck veins distend and she becomes dyspneic.
oneliner: 60F, long-standing neck swelling, lower edge not palpable + raised arms cause facial flushing, dyspnea → ?
ask: Which neck mass best explains this sign?

whyNot.A: A thyroglossal cyst rises with tongue protrusion; it does not **obstruct the thoracic inlet**
whyNot.C: A branchial cleft cyst is lateral; she has **venous obstruction on arm raising**
whyNot.D: Parathyroid adenoma is rarely palpable and does not cause **venous obstruction**
whyNot.E: Papillary carcinoma is a firm nodule; her **plethora comes from inlet obstruction**

why: A goiter extending behind the sternum obstructs the thoracic inlet when the arms are raised, producing facial plethora and venous distension (Pemberton sign).

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Upper lid lags as eye looks down
Arms raised cause facial flushing, distress
Bruit heard over diffusely enlarged thyroid

idea.rule: Raised arms cause facial flushing = thyroid mass at the thoracic inlet.
also: Check for superior vena cava compression

set_title: Endocrine body habitus signs: Moon facies, Buffalo hump, Purple striae, Palmar crease hyperpigmentation and Spade-like hands
stem: A 36-year-old woman with 6 months of weight gain has hypertension and bruises easily. Wide, dark red-blue stretch marks cover her lower abdomen and flanks.
oneliner: 36F, weight gain, hypertension, easy bruising + wide dark stretch marks on abdomen → ?

whyNot.A: Moon facies is a round face; her finding is on the **abdomen and flanks**
whyNot.B: Buffalo hump is an upper back fat pad; her finding is **abdominal stretch marks**
whyNot.C: Palmar crease darkening occurs in adrenal insufficiency; she has **wide abdominal stretch marks**
whyNot.D: Spade-like hands are enlarged hands in acromegaly; her finding is on the **abdomen**

why: Wide violaceous abdominal striae reflect cortisol excess, which thins skin and breaks down collagen, letting underlying vessels show through.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Large thick hands, rings no longer fit

idea.rule: Wide abdominal striae with bruising = cortisol excess.
also: Normal pregnancy striae are pale and thin

set_title: Endocrine body habitus signs: Moon facies, Buffalo hump, Purple striae, Palmar crease hyperpigmentation and Spade-like hands
stem: A 44-year-old man says his wedding ring no longer fits and his shoe size has grown over 3 years. His hands are broad and thick with blunt fingertips, and his jaw protrudes.
oneliner: 44M, ring no longer fits + broad thick hands + protruding jaw → ?

whyNot.A: Moon facies is a round face; his main finding is **broad thick hands**
whyNot.B: Buffalo hump is an upper back fat pad; his finding is **enlarged hands**
whyNot.C: Purple striae are abdominal stretch marks; his finding is **blunt, thick hands**
whyNot.D: Palmar crease darkening is pigmentation; his hands are **enlarged, not dark**

why: Large, thick hands with blunt fingers are spade-like hands, typical of acromegaly from growth hormone excess, usually from a pituitary adenoma.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Large thick hands, rings no longer fit

idea.rule: Enlarging hands and shoes with jaw growth = acromegaly.
also: Check IGF-1, then glucose suppression test

set_title: Endocrine body habitus signs: Moon facies, Buffalo hump, Purple striae, Palmar crease hyperpigmentation and Spade-like hands
stem: A thin 30-year-old woman has fatigue, anorexia and blood pressure of 88/56 mm Hg. Her palmar creases and gums are darkened.
oneliner: 30F, fatigue, hypotension + dark palmar creases and gums → ?
ask: Which hormone is elevated and causes this darkening?

whyNot.A: Cortisol is **low** in adrenal insufficiency and does not darken skin
whyNot.C: Aldosterone is low in primary insufficiency; she has **hypotension from deficiency**
whyNot.D: Epinephrine does not stimulate melanocytes; her **darkening reflects POMC products**
whyNot.E: TSH does not cause **pigmentation of creases and gums**

why: In primary adrenal insufficiency, low cortisol removes feedback, so ACTH rises. POMC cleavage also yields MSH, which darkens palmar creases and gums.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Large thick hands, rings no longer fit

idea.rule: Dark creases and gums in adrenal failure = high ACTH (with MSH).

set_title: Endocrine body habitus signs: Moon facies, Buffalo hump, Purple striae, Palmar crease hyperpigmentation and Spade-like hands
stem: A 52-year-old man taking prednisone 40 mg daily for 8 months develops a fat pad over his upper back and a rounded face.
oneliner: 52M, 8 months of prednisone + upper back fat pad and round face → ?
ask: Which mechanism best explains this finding?

whyNot.B: Insulin deficiency causes weight loss; he has **gained central fat**
whyNot.C: Fluid retention causes edema and hypertension, not a **fixed upper back fat pad**
whyNot.D: Growth hormone enlarges hands and jaw; he has **a steroid exposure history**
whyNot.E: Thyroid hormone excess causes weight loss; he has **steroid-related fat gain**

why: Glucocorticoids shift fat to the trunk, face and dorsocervical area, forming a buffalo hump, while peripheral fat and muscle waste away.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Large thick hands, rings no longer fit

idea.rule: Chronic steroids shift fat centrally = buffalo hump and moon face.
also: Limbs thin as muscle breaks down
Same effect from endogenous cortisol excess

set_title: Newborn dysmorphic clues: Single palmar crease, Rocker-bottom feet, Overlapping clenched fingers, Short fourth and fifth metacarpals, Webbed neck and Cleft lip with polydactyly
stem: A 10-year-old girl with round face, short stature and obesity has depressed fourth and fifth knuckles when she makes a fist. Calcium is 6.9 mg/dL, phosphate 6.2 mg/dL and PTH is elevated.
oneliner: 10F, round face, short stature + short 4th, 5th knuckles, low calcium, high PTH → ?
ask: Which condition best explains these findings?

whyNot.A: Turner has short metacarpals but **normal PTH and calcium**
whyNot.C: Hypoparathyroidism has low PTH; hers is **high PTH**
whyNot.D: Rickets has low phosphate; hers is **high at 6.2 mg/dL**
whyNot.E: Kidney disease would not explain **short 4th and 5th metacarpals with round face**

why: Short fourth and fifth metacarpals with hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia and high PTH indicate Albright osteodystrophy of pseudohypoparathyroidism: end-organ PTH resistance (Gs-alpha defect).

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Fists clenched, index over middle finger
Knuckles 4 and 5 missing in a fist
Loose skin folds from neck to shoulders

idea.rule: Short 4th-5th metacarpals + low calcium + high PTH = pseudohypoparathyroidism.

set_title: Skin signs of internal disease: Trousseau sign of malignancy, Leser-Trelat sign, Acanthosis nigricans, Necrolytic migratory erythema and Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
stem: A 15-year-old girl with BMI 34 kg/m2 has velvety, hyperpigmented plaques on the posterior neck and axillae. She has irregular menses and acne.
oneliner: 15F, BMI 34 + velvety dark neck and axillary plaques + irregular menses → ?
ask: Which underlying state best explains this finding?

whyNot.A: Adrenal insufficiency tans skin diffusely, not **velvety plaques with obesity**
whyNot.B: Hemochromatosis gives smooth bronze skin; she has **velvety neck plaques**
whyNot.D: That causes depigmented patches (vitiligo), but hers are **hyperpigmented**
whyNot.E: Sun exposure tans exposed areas; hers are **flexural velvety plaques**

why: Velvety dark plaques of the neck and axillae are acanthosis nigricans; hyperinsulinemia stimulates keratinocytes and fibroblasts through IGF-1 receptors in **obesity**.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Sudden eruption of many seborrheic keratoses
Velvety dark plaques in neck, axillae
Insulin resistance; abrupt onset: gastric adenocarcinoma
Spreading red blistering rash, groin, face
Clubbing with painful periostitis of long bones

idea.rule: Velvety flexural plaques + obesity = acanthosis nigricans from insulin resistance.
also: Sudden onset in adults: gastric adenocarcinoma
PCOS and type 2 diabetes are common

set_title: Skin signs of internal disease: Trousseau sign of malignancy, Leser-Trelat sign, Acanthosis nigricans, Necrolytic migratory erythema and Hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
stem: A 56-year-old woman has 4 months of weight loss, new diabetes mellitus and a painful spreading red rash with blisters and crusting in the groin and around the mouth. Glucose is 240 mg/dL. CT shows a 4-cm mass in the pancreatic tail.
oneliner: 56F, weight loss + new diabetes + blistering groin and perioral rash → ?
ask: Which tumor best explains this rash?

whyNot.A: Insulinoma causes hypoglycemia; she has **glucose 240 mg/dL**
whyNot.B: Somatostatinoma causes diabetes, gallstones and steatorrhea, not a **migratory blistering rash**
whyNot.C: VIPoma causes profuse watery diarrhea and hypokalemia, not a **blistering rash**
whyNot.E: Gastrinoma causes refractory ulcers and diarrhea, not a **blistering rash with diabetes**

why: A spreading blistering groin and perioral rash with **new diabetes** and weight loss is necrolytic migratory erythema from a glucagon-secreting pancreatic tumor.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Sudden eruption of many seborrheic keratoses
Velvety dark plaques in neck, axillae
Insulin resistance; abrupt onset: gastric adenocarcinoma
Spreading red blistering rash, groin, face
Clubbing with painful periostitis of long bones

idea.rule: New diabetes + weight loss + migratory blistering rash = glucagonoma.
also: Zinc and amino acid deficiency contribute

set_title: Odor clues: Fruity breath, Fetor hepaticus, Bitter almond odor, Garlic odor, Musty (mousy) body odor and Maple syrup urine
stem: A 17-year-old girl has 2 days of vomiting, abdominal pain and deep, rapid respirations after 3 weeks of polyuria and a 5-kg weight loss. Her exhaled air smells sweet, like nail-polish remover. Glucose is 540 mg/dL.
oneliner: 17F, polyuria + weight loss + deep breathing + sweet acetone breath → ?

whyNot.A: Fetor hepaticus comes with liver failure; she has **polyuria and glucose 540**
whyNot.B: Bitter almond odor means cyanide, without **hyperglycemia and polyuria**
whyNot.D: Garlic odor suggests organophosphate or arsenic, not **polyuria with hyperglycemia**
whyNot.E: Musty odor is phenylketonuria in infants; she is **17 with hyperglycemia**

why: A sweet, acetone-like breath odor is fruity breath from ketones in diabetic ketoacidosis; **glucose 540 with deep breathing** confirms it.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Musty smell of urine and sweat

idea.rule: Sweet acetone breath + hyperglycemia + deep breathing = ketones of DKA.
also: Acetone is exhaled by the lungs

set_title: Breathing patterns: Kussmaul, Cheyne-Stokes, Biot, apneustic and central neurogenic
stem: A 19-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes has had 2 days of vomiting and abdominal pain after running out of insulin. Her breath smells fruity. She takes deep, rapid, regular breaths at 32/min. Glucose is 540 mg/dL, arterial pH 7.06, PCO2 16 mm Hg and bicarbonate 5 mEq/L.
oneliner: 19F, type 1 diabetes, out of insulin + deep, rapid, regular breaths, pH 7.06 → ?

whyNot.A: Cheyne-Stokes waxes, wanes and pauses; hers are **deep, rapid and regular**
whyNot.B: Biot breathing is irregular with pauses; hers is **regular at 32/min**
whyNot.D: Apneustic breathing holds each inspiration; she breathes **rapidly at 32/min**
whyNot.E: Central neurogenic hyperventilation has no acidosis; she has **pH 7.06, bicarbonate 5**

why: Deep, fast, regular breaths are Kussmaul breathing. Acid stimulates the peripheral chemoreceptors, so she blows off CO2 to offset the ketoacidosis.

head: What it is
Classic cause
rows: Breaths swell, fade, then pause; repeats
Irregular breaths and pauses, no pattern
Lower pons lesion, e.g. basilar stroke
Fast deep breaths without metabolic acidosis

idea.rule: Deep, fast, regular breathing plus low bicarbonate = Kussmaul, compensating for metabolic acidosis.
also: Check compensation with the Winter formula
Also seen in uremia and lactic acidosis
